details.summary:
Uttari Betta Sunrise Trek – A Quick Escape into the Hills

Just a short journey from Bengaluru, Uttari Betta, also known as Hutridurga, offers an easy and refreshing introduction to the hills of Tumakuru district. The trail brings together rocky terrain, open landscapes and historic surroundings, making it a convenient choice for travellers looking for a quick break from the city.

The trek begins during the early hours, when the surroundings are calm and the trail is less crowded. As you make your way across the rocky sections, the gradual climb keeps the experience engaging without making it overly demanding. With an approximate trekking distance of 5 km, the route can be completed in around 1 hour 30 minutes, depending on group pace and trail conditions.

As you approach the summit, the landscape opens up and the early morning light begins to transform the surrounding countryside. Reaching the top around sunrise gives you an opportunity to enjoy expansive views across the nearby hills and open terrain.

With its easy difficulty level and relatively short trekking duration, Uttari Betta is suitable for beginners with a reasonable level of fitness as well as experienced trekkers looking for a relaxed weekend outing. The combination of a simple climb, sunrise views and historical surroundings makes it a memorable escape from Bengaluru.

Whether you're stepping into trekking for the first time or simply looking for a peaceful morning in the hills, Uttari Betta offers an enjoyable outdoor experience without requiring an entire day on the trail.

activities.description: Reach the designated starting point and prepare for the trek. After a short briefing from the trek leader, get your essentials ready for the climb.

activities.title: Early Morning | Begin the Trek
activities.description: Start walking towards the summit under the early morning sky. The trail features rocky sections and a gradual ascent through the hill landscape.

activities.description: As you gain elevation, the surroundings begin to brighten. Continue towards the top while enjoying the changing views around the hill.

sections.title: A Trek with History & Scenic Views
sections.body:
Uttari Betta, also known as Hutridurga, combines natural scenery with historical elements. The hill is home to the remains of an old fort along with the Shankareswar Temple, giving the route more character than a typical sunrise viewpoint.

As you explore the summit, the rocky landscape and panoramic countryside views provide a scenic backdrop, while the historic structures add another dimension to the trekking experience. Together, these elements make Uttari Betta a compact trek where adventure, nature and heritage come together.

sections.title: Things to carry
sections.body:
Things to Carry for Uttari Betta Trek

(Since the trek begins during the early hours, packing the right essentials is important.)

[Must Carry]
• Small trekking backpack
• At least 2 litres of drinking water
• Headlamp or torch
• Trekking shoes with good grip
• Light jacket or windcheater
• Extra pair of socks
• Cap
• Sunglasses
• Sunscreen
• Energy bars or dry fruits
• Personal medication
• Fully charged mobile phone

• Power bank
• Valid government-issued ID

[During Monsoon]
• Rain jacket or poncho
• Waterproof backpack cover
• Waterproof phone pouch
• Extra clothes and socks

Packing Tip

Keep your backpack light. Avoid carrying unnecessary items as you'll be walking for several hours over uneven terrain.

sections.title: Trail guidelines
sections.body:
Uttari Betta is a natural and historical destination. Help preserve it for future travellers.

"Trek Responsibly. Respect the Hills."

• Follow your trek leader's instructions at all times.
• Follow Forest Department/local rules and restrictions where applicable.
• Stay with the group throughout the trek.
• Remain on the designated trekking trail.
• Do not litter.
• Carry all waste back with you.
• Avoid single-use plastic.
• Do not smoke or consume alcohol during the trek.
• Do not light fires or campfires.
• Do not disturb wildlife.
• Do not damage plants or historical structures.
• Be careful around steep and rocky sections.
• Avoid standing too close to edges while taking photographs.
• Wear appropriate trekking footwear.
• Stay hydrated throughout the trek.
• Take breaks whenever required.
• Avoid loud music that may disturb wildlife and fellow trekkers.

"Leave Only Footprints. Take Only Memories."
